offer.say: Rhonda Pelkey. I stop things. Mostly balls, sometimes Kev. Carnival weekend is the broomball final and the ice has to be flat. Last year the corner by the visitors' gate ate a sneaker. Ate it. We heard it squeak.

options.text: Flat ice for the final. Done.
Does broomball really care about ice?
Carnival's already a lot. Can you play on whatever's there?

boot.say: The Golden Boot. 2003. Somebody's dad's rubber boot and a can of gold paint. It's been on my porch three years because nobody beats us. My neighbour thinks I'm a fishing champion.

options.text: Let's give it a final worth winning.

care.say: Do sneakers care? Yes. Do knees care? Very much. Does the crowd care? There's a crowd, {owner}. Carnival night, people come. With lanterns.

options.text: Then the crowd gets good ice.

decline.say: Whatever's there ate a sneaker. But okay. We're broomball. We forgive.

accepted.say: Corners first. The visitors' gate corner. It sweats. Earl knows.

p_edge.say: Earl says the edger starts on the third pull. I've seen it go to nine. I counted out loud. He didn't like that.

p_carnival.say: The Molars are carving a molar. They carve a molar every year. It's a very good molar.

complete.say: We LOST. In overtime! To the Smoke Eaters' wives' team! First time in three years! I've never been happier to lose anything. The Boot needs a new home, and it's not my porch. Where does it go?

options.text: The trophy case. Beside the pike.
With the winners, like a real trophy.
Back on your porch. You'll win it back.

c_case.say: Beside the surprised pike! It looks surprised too. It's a boot, it doesn't have a face, but it looks surprised.

c_winners.say: The Smoke Eaters' wives will put it in the fire hall. Good. Next year I'm going to the fire hall to get it back.

c_porch.say: Ha! My neighbour will be so relieved. Fishing champion, back in business.

done.say: Next carnival. I'm coming for that Boot.
